title: Non-blocking finding from PR #418's review (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups)
description: pr-reviewer accepted PR #418 (the root-absolute-specifier fix plus extraction of the e2e-import-guard/no-restricted-src-import rule into frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.js with a persisted vitest test). While independently re-verifying the PR, pr-reviewer found that one of the decision entry's two stated empirical justifications for keeping the extracted module as plain JS (rather than real TypeScript) does not hold on this repo's actual dev-container Node version, and that the resulting test file is genuinely unchecked by the frontend's static-verify gate -- non-blocking (the PR's own functionality, tests, lint, and type-check all pass; this is a gap in defense-in-depth, not a correctness bug in the shipped change), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's rule that every non-blocking finding gets a tracked follow-up task.

checklist.step: The decisions entry on frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups-followups claims (as one of two reasons the extracted rule module was kept as plain JS with JSDoc types rather than converted to real TypeScript): 'a sibling .ts file here would fail to load under plain Node ESM when eslint.config.js imports it directly (verified empirically: yarn lint with this file renamed to .ts throws a syntax error at the type-annotation tokens before any rule runs)'. Re-ran that exact experiment in this repo's actual dev container (node --version: v22.23.2, confirmed via `node --help` that `--no-experimental-strip-types` exists, i.e. type-stripping is ON by default in this Node version): renamed frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.js to .ts (content unchanged, updated eslint.config.js's import specifier to match) and ran `yarn lint` -- it passed cleanly, no syntax error. Went further and appended genuine (non-JSDoc) TypeScript syntax to the renamed file -- a typed function signature, an `interface`, a `type` alias, and a generic function -- and both `yarn lint` and a direct `node -e "import(...)"` probe loaded it without error. So the claimed empirical verification does not hold on this toolchain: Node's native type-stripping (on by default here) handles a plain-erasable-syntax .ts sibling file fine regardless of ESLint's own entry-file-only transpilation behavior, and this project's tsconfig.app.json/tsconfig.node.json already set `erasableSyntaxOnly: true` project-wide, i.e. exactly the syntax subset Node's stripping supports. The other stated reason (mirroring eslint.config.js's own pre-existing untyped/tsconfig-excluded status) still stands on its own and may well have been sufficient by itself -- but the decision entry's specific Node/ESM-loader empirical claim is factually wrong for this repo as it stands today and should be corrected (per CLAUDE.md's append-only correction convention: a fresh decisions entry noting the correction, not an in-place edit of the original text, since this doesn't meet the narrow in-place-edit carve-out).

Because frontend/eslint-rules/ sits outside both tsconfig.app.json's (`include: ["src", "tests", ".storybook"]`) and tsconfig.node.json's (`include: ["vite.config.ts", "playwright.config.ts"]`) project graphs, the new frontend/eslint-rules/no-restricted-src-import.test.ts -- a genuine TypeScript file with real type annotations (e.g. `Array<[label: string, source: string, blocked: boolean]>`, a type-cast in the wiring test) -- is never type-checked by `yarn tsc -b --noEmit`, and eslint's own config only applies `tseslint.configs.recommended` (not a type-aware `recommendedTypeChecked`) to it, so eslint doesn't catch type errors there either. Verified concretely: changed one test-table call from `isBlockedSrcSource(source)` to `isBlockedSrcSource(42)` (passing a `number` where the function's JSDoc/real signature expects a `string`) -- both `yarn lint` and `yarn tsc -b --noEmit` stayed clean (exit 0, no findings), and the bug was only caught by actually running `yarn vitest run eslint-rules` (which failed loudly with a runtime TypeError, since `isBlockedSrcSource` calls `.startsWith()` on the argument). In this specific case the runtime failure is immediate and loud, but the general risk -- a type error or wrong import in this test file going unnoticed by the repo's own static-verify gate, the exact 'trap' scenario this task's own review was asked to check for -- is real, not hypothetical, given Node's native stripping would in fact let a tsconfig-included version of this exact file (and the .js module, converted to .ts) type-check cleanly today. Worth deciding whether to add frontend/eslint-rules/ to tsconfig.app.json's include (or a small dedicated tsconfig project) now that the Node-loader objection to doing so doesn't hold, closing this gap for both the rule module and its test.
